en.g: Describe how people do things with adverbs of manner.
p: Most adverbs add -ly to the adjective: quick becomes quickly, careful becomes carefully.
Some are irregular: good becomes well, fast stays fast, hard stays hard.
Adverbs usually go after the verb or object: She speaks English slowly.
en.q: How do you do things? Tell me something you do well and something you do slowly.
en.c: Describe five people you know with adverbs: how they talk, drive, cook, sing or work.

de.g: Du beschreibst mit Adverbien, wie Menschen etwas tun.
p: Die meisten Adverbien hängen -ly an das Adjektiv: quick wird quickly, careful wird carefully.
Manche sind unregelmäßig: good wird well, fast bleibt fast, hard bleibt hard.
Adverbien stehen meist nach Verb oder Objekt: She speaks English slowly.
de.q: Wie machst du Dinge? Nenn mir etwas, das du gut, und etwas, das du langsam machst.
de.c: Beschreib fünf Menschen mit Adverbien: wie sie sprechen, fahren, kochen, singen oder arbeiten.

es.g: Describe cómo hace la gente las cosas con adverbios de modo.
p: Casi todos añaden -ly al adjetivo: quick pasa a quickly, careful a carefully.
Algunos son irregulares: good pasa a well, fast sigue fast, hard sigue hard.
Suelen ir después del verbo o del complemento: She speaks English slowly.
es.q: ¿Cómo haces las cosas? Dime algo que haces bien y algo que haces despacio.
es.c: Describe a cinco personas con adverbios: cómo hablan, conducen, cocinan, cantan o trabajan.

fr.g: Décrire comment les gens font les choses avec les adverbes de manière.
p: La plupart ajoutent -ly à l'adjectif : quick devient quickly, careful devient carefully.
Certains sont irréguliers : good devient well, fast reste fast, hard reste hard.
L'adverbe se place souvent après le verbe ou le complément : She speaks English slowly.
fr.q: Comment fais-tu les choses ? Dis-moi une chose que tu fais bien et une que tu fais lentement.
fr.c: Décris cinq personnes avec des adverbes : comment elles parlent, conduisent, cuisinent, chantent ou travaillent.

it.g: Descrivi come le persone fanno le cose con gli avverbi di modo.
p: Quasi tutti aggiungono -ly all'aggettivo: quick diventa quickly, careful diventa carefully.
Alcuni sono irregolari: good diventa well, fast resta fast, hard resta hard.
Di solito vanno dopo il verbo o il complemento: She speaks English slowly.
it.q: Come fai le cose? Dimmi una cosa che fai bene e una che fai lentamente.
it.c: Descrivi cinque persone con gli avverbi: come parlano, guidano, cucinano, cantano o lavorano.

pt.g: Descreve como as pessoas fazem as coisas com advérbios de modo.
p: A maioria junta -ly ao adjetivo: quick fica quickly, careful fica carefully.
Alguns são irregulares: good fica well, fast fica fast, hard fica hard.
Costumam vir depois do verbo ou do complemento: She speaks English slowly.
pt.q: Como fazes as coisas? Diz-me algo que fazes bem e algo que fazes devagar.
pt.c: Descreve cinco pessoas com advérbios: como falam, conduzem, cozinham, cantam ou trabalham.

pt_BR.g: Descreva como as pessoas fazem as coisas com advérbios de modo.
p: A maioria ganha -ly no adjetivo: quick vira quickly, careful vira carefully.
Alguns são irregulares: good vira well, fast continua fast, hard continua hard.
Costumam vir depois do verbo ou do complemento: She speaks English slowly.
pt_BR.q: Como você faz as coisas? Me diga algo que faz bem e algo que faz devagar.
pt_BR.c: Descreva cinco pessoas com advérbios: como falam, dirigem, cozinham, cantam ou trabalham.

vocab.ex: He finished his lunch quickly.
Can you speak more slowly, please?
Drive carefully, the road is wet.
She plays the piano very well.
My brother runs really fast.
They work hard every day.

target.gram: Adverbs of manner: adjective + -ly (slow-slowly). Irregular: good-well, fast-fast, hard-hard. Position: after the verb/object.

en.g: Say when something is more or less than you need.
p: Too plus adjective means more than you want: It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Adjective plus enough means sufficient: I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough plus noun: We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
en.q: Think of something you didn't buy or do. Was it too expensive, or were you not ready enough?
en.c: Write six sentences about your life now, three with too and three with enough.

de.g: Du sagst, wann etwas mehr oder weniger ist als nötig.
p: Too plus Adjektiv heißt zu viel: It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Adjektiv plus enough heißt genug: I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough plus Nomen: We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
de.q: Denk an etwas, das du nicht gekauft oder gemacht hast. War es too expensive oder warst du nicht bereit genug?
de.c: Schreib sechs Sätze über dein Leben jetzt, drei mit too und drei mit enough.

es.g: Di cuándo algo es más o menos de lo que necesitas.
p: Too más adjetivo significa demasiado: It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Adjetivo más enough significa suficiente: I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough más sustantivo: We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
es.q: Piensa en algo que no compraste o no hiciste. ¿Era too expensive o no estabas listo?
es.c: Escribe seis frases sobre tu vida ahora, tres con too y tres con enough.

fr.g: Dire quand quelque chose est trop ou pas assez.
p: Too plus adjectif veut dire trop : It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Adjectif plus enough veut dire assez : I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough plus nom : We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
fr.q: Pense à une chose que tu n'as pas achetée ou faite. C'était too expensive, ou tu n'étais pas prêt ?
fr.c: Écris six phrases sur ta vie actuelle, trois avec too et trois avec enough.

it.g: Dici quando qualcosa è più o meno di quanto serve.
p: Too più aggettivo vuol dire troppo: It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Aggettivo più enough vuol dire abbastanza: I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough più nome: We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
it.q: Pensa a qualcosa che non hai comprato o fatto. Era too expensive o non eri pronto?
it.c: Scrivi sei frasi sulla tua vita di adesso, tre con too e tre con enough.

pt.g: Diz quando algo é mais ou menos do que precisas.
p: Too mais adjetivo significa demasiado: It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Adjetivo mais enough significa suficiente: I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough mais nome: We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
pt.q: Pensa em algo que não compraste ou não fizeste. Era too expensive ou não estavas preparado?
pt.c: Escreve seis frases sobre a tua vida agora, três com too e três com enough.

pt_BR.g: Diga quando algo é mais ou menos do que você precisa.
p: Too mais adjetivo significa demais: It's too expensive. It's too cold.
Adjetivo mais enough significa suficiente: I'm not old enough. Is it warm enough?
Enough mais substantivo: We don't have enough time. There are enough chairs.
pt_BR.q: Pense em algo que você não comprou ou não fez. Era too expensive ou você não estava pronto?
pt_BR.c: Escreva seis frases sobre sua vida agora, três com too e três com enough.

vocab.ex: This phone is too expensive for me.
It's too cold to swim today.
She isn't old enough to drive.
Is this bag big enough?
We don't have enough time for lunch.
I ate too much cake!

target.gram: too + adjective (too hot = more than OK), adjective + enough (warm enough), enough + noun (enough money).

en.t: Quantifiers: a lot of, a few, a little
en.g: Talk about amounts naturally with common quantifiers.
p: A lot of works with everything: a lot of friends, a lot of time.
Many and a few go with countable nouns: many books, a few people.
Much and a little go with uncountable nouns: much money (in questions and negatives), a little sugar.
en.q: How much free time do you have during the week? A lot, a little or not much?
en.c: Describe your kitchen or bag in six sentences with a lot of, a few, a little, much and many.

de.t: Mengenwörter: a lot of, a few, a little
de.g: Du sprichst natürlich über Mengen mit häufigen Mengenwörtern.
p: A lot of passt zu allem: a lot of friends, a lot of time.
Many und a few stehen bei zählbaren Nomen: many books, a few people.
Much und a little bei unzählbaren: much money (in Fragen und Verneinungen), a little sugar.
de.q: Wie viel Freizeit hast du unter der Woche? A lot, a little oder not much?
de.c: Beschreib deine Küche oder Tasche in sechs Sätzen mit a lot of, a few, a little, much und many.

es.t: Cuantificadores: a lot of, a few, a little
es.g: Habla de cantidades con naturalidad usando cuantificadores comunes.
p: A lot of vale para todo: a lot of friends, a lot of time.
Many y a few van con contables: many books, a few people.
Much y a little van con incontables: much money (en preguntas y negativas), a little sugar.
es.q: ¿Cuánto tiempo libre tienes entre semana? ¿A lot, a little o not much?
es.c: Describe tu cocina o tu bolso en seis frases con a lot of, a few, a little, much y many.

fr.t: Quantifieurs : a lot of, a few, a little
fr.g: Parler naturellement des quantités avec les quantifieurs courants.
p: A lot of va avec tout : a lot of friends, a lot of time.
Many et a few vont avec les noms dénombrables : many books, a few people.
Much et a little avec les indénombrables : much money (questions et négations), a little sugar.
fr.q: Combien de temps libre as-tu en semaine ? A lot, a little ou not much ?
fr.c: Décris ta cuisine ou ton sac en six phrases avec a lot of, a few, a little, much et many.

it.t: Quantificatori: a lot of, a few, a little
it.g: Parli di quantità in modo naturale con i quantificatori più comuni.
p: A lot of va bene con tutto: a lot of friends, a lot of time.
Many e a few vanno con i numerabili: many books, a few people.
Much e a little con i non numerabili: much money (domande e negative), a little sugar.
it.q: Quanto tempo libero hai durante la settimana? A lot, a little o not much?
it.c: Descrivi la tua cucina o la tua borsa in sei frasi con a lot of, a few, a little, much e many.

pt.t: Quantificadores: a lot of, a few, a little
pt.g: Fala de quantidades com naturalidade usando quantificadores comuns.
p: A lot of serve para tudo: a lot of friends, a lot of time.
Many e a few vão com contáveis: many books, a few people.
Much e a little vão com incontáveis: much money (em perguntas e negativas), a little sugar.

pt.c: Descreve a tua cozinha ou a tua mala em seis frases com a lot of, a few, a little, much e many.

pt_BR.t: Quantificadores: a lot of, a few, a little

vocab.ex: I have a lot of friends in this city.
There aren't many shops in my village.
I don't have much time today.
I invited a few friends for dinner.

target.gram: Countable: many, a few (many books). Uncountable: much, a little (a little sugar). Both: a lot of. Much is common in questions/negatives.

en.g: Use some-, any-, no- and every- words for people, things and places.
p: Some- in positive sentences: I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- in questions and negatives: Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.
No- already means not: Nobody called. Every- means all: Everyone is here.
en.q: Did you do anything special yesterday, or did you go nowhere at all?
en.c: Write six sentences about your weekend, each with a different some-, any-, no- or every- word.

de.g: Du nutzt Wörter mit some-, any-, no- und every- für Personen, Dinge und Orte.
p: Some- in bejahten Sätzen: I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- in Fragen und Verneinungen: Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.
No- ist schon verneint: Nobody called. Every- heißt alle: Everyone is here.
de.q: Hast du gestern etwas Besonderes gemacht, oder warst du nirgendwo?
de.c: Schreib sechs Sätze über dein Wochenende, jeder mit einem anderen some-, any-, no- oder every-Wort.

es.g: Usa palabras con some-, any-, no- y every- para personas, cosas y lugares.
p: Some- en frases afirmativas: I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- en preguntas y negativas: Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.
No- ya es negativo: Nobody called. Every- significa todos: Everyone is here.
es.q: ¿Hiciste algo especial ayer o no fuiste a ningún sitio?
es.c: Escribe seis frases sobre tu fin de semana, cada una con una palabra distinta de some-, any-, no- o every-.

fr.g: Utiliser les mots en some-, any-, no- et every- pour les personnes, choses et lieux.
p: Some- dans les phrases affirmatives : I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- dans les questions et négations : Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.
No- est déjà négatif : Nobody called. Every- veut dire tous : Everyone is here.
fr.q: As-tu fait quelque chose de spécial hier, ou tu n'es allé nulle part ?
fr.c: Écris six phrases sur ton week-end, chacune avec un mot différent en some-, any-, no- ou every-.

it.g: Usi le parole con some-, any-, no- ed every- per persone, cose e luoghi.
p: Some- nelle frasi affermative: I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- nelle domande e nelle negative: Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.
No- è già negativo: Nobody called. Every- vuol dire tutti: Everyone is here.
it.q: Ieri hai fatto qualcosa di speciale o non sei andato da nessuna parte?
it.c: Scrivi sei frasi sul tuo weekend, ognuna con una parola diversa in some-, any-, no- o every-.

pt.g: Usa palavras com some-, any-, no- e every- para pessoas, coisas e lugares.
p: Some- em frases afirmativas: I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- em perguntas e negativas: Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.
No- já é negativo: Nobody called. Every- quer dizer todos: Everyone is here.
pt.q: Fizeste alguma coisa especial ontem ou não foste a lado nenhum?
pt.c: Escreve seis frases sobre o teu fim de semana, cada uma com uma palavra diferente em some-, any-, no- ou every-.

pt_BR.g: Use palavras com some-, any-, no- e every- para pessoas, coisas e lugares.
p: Some- em frases afirmativas: I saw someone. I want something to eat.
Any- em perguntas e negativas: Is anybody there? I didn't go anywhere.

I'd like something to drink.

Nobody answered the phone.
Everyone loved the cake.

target.gram: some- (positive), any- (questions/negatives), no- (already negative: Nobody came), every- (all). + -one/-body, -thing, -where.

en.t: Phrasal verbs: get up, turn on
en.g: Learn your first everyday phrasal verbs.
p: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word, with a new meaning: get up, wake up.
Turn on and turn off are for lights and machines: Turn off the TV, please.
Put on is for clothes: Put on your coat. Its opposite is take off.
en.q: Tell me your morning routine using wake up, get up, turn on and put on.
en.c: Write your morning in six steps, each with a phrasal verb, and say it aloud.

de.t: Phrasal verbs: get up, turn on
de.g: Du lernst deine ersten alltäglichen phrasal verbs.
p: Ein phrasal verb ist Verb plus kleines Wort mit neuer Bedeutung: get up, wake up.
Turn on und turn off für Licht und Geräte: Turn off the TV, please.
Put on für Kleidung: Put on your coat. Das Gegenteil ist take off.
de.q: Erzähl mir deine Morgenroutine mit wake up, get up, turn on und put on.
de.c: Schreib deinen Morgen in sechs Schritten, jeder mit einem phrasal verb, und sprich ihn laut.

es.t: Phrasal verbs: get up, turn on
es.g: Aprende tus primeros phrasal verbs del día a día.
p: Un phrasal verb es verbo más una palabrita, con un significado nuevo: get up, wake up.
Turn on y turn off sirven para luces y aparatos: Turn off the TV, please.
Put on es para la ropa: Put on your coat. Lo contrario es take off.
es.q: Cuéntame tu rutina de la mañana con wake up, get up, turn on y put on.
es.c: Escribe tu mañana en seis pasos, cada uno con un phrasal verb, y dilo en voz alta.

fr.t: Phrasal verbs : get up, turn on

Turn on et turn off pour la lumière et les appareils : Turn off the TV, please.
Put on pour les vêtements : Put on your coat. Le contraire, c'est take off.
fr.q: Raconte-moi ta routine du matin avec wake up, get up, turn on et put on.
fr.c: Écris ta matinée en six étapes, chacune avec un phrasal verb, et dis-la à voix haute.

en.g: Talk about chores with natural phrasal verbs.
p: Clean up means make a place tidy: Let's clean up the kitchen.
Wash up means wash the dishes, throw away means put in the bin: Throw away that old bread.
Pick up means lift from the floor, look for means try to find: I'm looking for my keys.
en.q: Which chore do you like most, and which one do you always leave for later?
en.c: Write a family chore list with six phrasal verbs and who does each job.

de.g: Du sprichst mit natürlichen phrasal verbs über Hausarbeit.
p: Clean up heißt aufräumen, sauber machen: Let's clean up the kitchen.
Wash up heißt abspülen, throw away heißt wegwerfen: Throw away that old bread.
Pick up heißt aufheben, look for heißt suchen: I'm looking for my keys.
de.q: Welche Hausarbeit magst du am liebsten, und welche schiebst du immer auf?
de.c: Schreib einen Haushaltsplan mit sechs phrasal verbs und wer welche Aufgabe macht.

es.g: Habla de las tareas de casa con phrasal verbs naturales.
p: Clean up es ordenar y limpiar un lugar: Let's clean up the kitchen.

Pick up es recoger del suelo, look for es buscar: I'm looking for my keys.
es.q: ¿Qué tarea de casa te gusta más y cuál dejas siempre para después?
es.c: Escribe una lista de tareas familiares con seis phrasal verbs y quién hace cada una.

fr.q: Quelle tâche ménagère préfères-tu, et laquelle remets-tu toujours à plus tard ?
fr.c: Écris une liste de tâches familiales avec six phrasal verbs et qui fait quoi.

en.g: Use make and do with the right words in common pairs.
p: Make is often for creating something: make a cake, make a plan, make a phone call.
Do is often for tasks and work: do homework, do the dishes, do exercise.
Some pairs you just learn: make a mistake, make friends, do your best, do someone a favour.
en.q: What do you usually do on Saturday mornings, and what do you like to make?
en.c: Make two lists, make and do, with five pairs each, and write a sentence for your favourite.

de.g: Du benutzt make und do mit den richtigen Wörtern in festen Paaren.
p: Make heißt oft etwas herstellen: make a cake, make a plan, make a phone call.
Do steht oft für Aufgaben und Arbeit: do homework, do the dishes, do exercise.
Manche Paare lernst du einfach: make a mistake, make friends, do your best, do someone a favour.
de.q: Was machst du meistens am Samstagmorgen, und was stellst du gern selbst her?
de.c: Mach zwei Listen, make und do, mit je fünf Paaren, und schreib einen Satz zu deinem Lieblingspaar.

es.g: Usa make y do con las palabras correctas en las parejas más comunes.
p: Make suele ser crear algo: make a cake, make a plan, make a phone call.
Do suele ser para tareas y trabajo: do homework, do the dishes, do exercise.
Algunas parejas hay que aprenderlas: make a mistake, make friends, do your best, do someone a favour.
es.q: ¿Qué sueles hacer los sábados por la mañana y qué te gusta preparar?
es.c: Haz dos listas, make y do, con cinco parejas cada una, y escribe una frase con tu favorita.

fr.g: Utiliser make et do avec les bons mots dans les associations courantes.
p: Make sert souvent à créer : make a cake, make a plan, make a phone call.
Do sert souvent pour les tâches et le travail : do homework, do the dishes, do exercise.
Certaines paires s'apprennent par cœur : make a mistake, make friends, do your best, do someone a favour.
fr.q: Que fais-tu d'habitude le samedi matin, et qu'aimes-tu préparer toi-même ?
fr.c: Fais deux listes, make et do, de cinq paires chacune, et écris une phrase avec ta préférée.

it.g: Usi make e do con le parole giuste nelle coppie più comuni.
p: Make spesso è creare qualcosa: make a cake, make a plan, make a phone call.
Do spesso è per compiti e lavori: do homework, do the dishes, do exercise.
Alcune coppie si imparano a memoria: make a mistake, make friends, do your best, do someone a favour.
it.q: Cosa fai di solito il sabato mattina e cosa ti piace preparare?
it.c: Fai due liste, make e do, con cinque coppie ciascuna, e scrivi una frase con la tua preferita.

pt.g: Usa make e do com as palavras certas nos pares mais comuns.

Do costuma ser para tarefas e trabalho: do homework, do the dishes, do exercise.
Alguns pares aprendem-se de cor: make a mistake, make friends, do your best, do someone a favour.
pt.q: O que costumas fazer ao sábado de manhã e o que gostas de preparar?
pt.c: Faz duas listas, make e do, com cinco pares cada, e escreve uma frase com o teu favorito.

en.g: Use say and tell correctly in everyday speech.
p: Say is about the words: She said hello. He said that he was tired.
Tell needs a person after it: She told me the news. Tell me about your day.
Fixed pairs with tell: tell a story, tell a joke, tell the truth, tell the time.
en.q: What is a funny story someone told you? What did they say?
en.c: Write three sentences with say and three with tell about conversations you had this week.

en.g: Describe how you feel and explain why.

Ask about feelings kindly: How are you feeling? Why are you so happy today?

en.g: Bring together past tenses, the present perfect, future forms and advice.
p: Past: I was walking when I saw... Experience: Have you ever...? I've been to...
Future: I'm going to (plan), I'll (decision), I'm meeting Ana at six (arrangement).
Advice and rules: you should, you have to, you don't have to, you mustn't.
